operator_io_quirks: Table/column names mixed case: department.Department_ID vs management.department_ID (FK child col spelled differently from parent); case-insensitive lookup required, original spelling preserved in DDL.

management PK is composite (Department_ID, head_ID) but DDL declares PRIMARY KEY ("Department_ID","head_ID") while column is named department_ID — pragma pk order vs name case mismatch; composite-PK member -> max_l0=30.
management.department_ID FK references department.Department_ID (case differs); pragma foreign_key_list parent col may be NULL -> same-name fallback would fail here, must use declared parent.
Tiny tables (15/10/5 rows): original_values lists are short; rng.choices(k=min(5,len)) draws with replacement from 5-15 values.
Creation is TEXT storing 4-digit years ('1789','1947'); declared type TEXT -> String fuzzer, NOT Date; text-stored dates not detected.
Budget_in_Billions REAL with wide range (9.96..439.3); Num_Employees REAL up to 3,000,000 — Number fuzzer scale=4 gives [-10^4,10^4], so fresh draws are far below 3e6.
age REAL but integer-valued (67.0,68.0); Number float perturbation +-0.01/+-0.02 keeps near-integers.
born_state has only 5 distinct values over 10 rows (duplicates); Name/name distinct=rows.
temporary_acting TEXT with 2 distinct ('Yes','No') — looks boolean but dispatches to String fuzzer.
No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere; only PKs and FKs — insert failures only from PK/FK (FK off) so few rows dropped.
No views/triggers/indexes in DDL; empty clone is just 3 CREATE TABLEs.
All declared types are INT/TEXT/REAL — no crash-fallback, no Date/Time/Bool/Bit dispatch on this DB.
operator_ts_expectations: department.Department_ID, head.head_ID: Number fuzzer, single-col PK -> max_l0=inf, fresh ints in [-10^4,10^4] perturbed +-1/+-2; PK dedup keeps first occurrence.

management composite PK: both members Number with max_l0=30; FK columns drawn from parent's FINAL filtered values with replacement -> many duplicate (dept,head) pairs dropped by sample_fresh_primary_keys.
Name/name: String fuzzer, charset a-zA-Z 0-9(), length [min,max+1] from 5 originals + pool; contaminate 50% -> implausible names like 'StateXq7' — likely FN source for name-equality predicates.
Creation: String fuzzer on 4-digit year strings; int-like strings get str(i+1)/str(i-1) added, so '1789'->'1790','1788' plausible; but fresh random strings also appear -> FN for year comparisons.
born_state: String fuzzer with only 5 originals; fresh random strings dominate -> state-name predicates miss.
temporary_acting: String fuzzer, 2 originals 'Yes'/'No' plus random strings -> boolean-like predicates (='Yes') often miss.
Budget_in_Billions/Num_Employees: Number scale=4, list_max quirk (min(el),10^4) — fresh draws in [min,10^4] not near 3e6; range predicates on large values likely FN.
Ranking: Number, 15 distinct 1..15; fresh ints in [-10^4,10^4] -> ranking comparisons (<=5) often miss.
age: Number float, originals 52..69; fresh uniform [-10^4,10^4] -> age predicates miss; perturbation keeps near-integers.
Small tables (5-15 rows) mean TS sizes (30..2500) vastly exceed originals -> joins produce many rows; aggregate predicates (COUNT, AVG) rarely match gold.

FK consistency: management rows always reference existing department/head after filtering, so join predicates on management are satisfiable; but department/head PKs are fresh random ints, so gold literal IDs (e.g. Department_ID=2) rarely present -> FN on ID equality.
No NULLs in original; TS may emit NULLs only via empty-parent FK path (unlikely here) — NOT NULL not enforced, so NULLs possible in non-PK columns.
